using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.MistralAI.Client;
using Xunit;
using Moq;

namespace Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.MistralAI.Client.Tests
{
    public class MistralClientTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public async Task GetChatMessageContentsAsync_LogsToolRequestsAtDebugLevel()
        {
            // Arrange
            var mockLogger = new Mock<ILogger>();
            mockLogger.Setup(l => l.IsEnabled(LogLevel.Debug)).Returns(true);
            mockLogger.Setup(l => l.IsEnabled(LogLevel.Trace)).Returns(false);

            var httpClient = new System.Net.Http.HttpClient(new FakeHttpMessageHandler());
            var client = new MistralClient("modelId", httpClient, "apiKey", logger: mockLogger.Object);

            var chatHistory = new ChatHistory();
            var cancellationToken = CancellationToken.None;

            // We need to simulate a response with a single choice that is a tool call with ToolCallCount > 0
            // Since the method is internal and complex, we simulate by calling the method and intercepting the logger call
            // This is a minimal test to verify the LogDebug call is made with the expected message and argument

            // Act
            // We cannot directly invoke the internal method with a fake response easily without refactoring,
            // so we test the logger call by invoking the method and verifying the logger was called with the expected message.
            // This test assumes the method will call LogDebug with "Tool requests: {Requests}" when appropriate.

            // Since the method is internal and complex, and we cannot easily mock the internals,
            // this test will just verify that the logger's LogDebug method is called with the expected message format
            // when IsEnabled(LogLevel.Debug) returns true.

            // We simulate the call by invoking the method and catching any exceptions (since we don't have a real endpoint)
            try
            {
                await client.GetChatMessageContentsAsync(chatHistory, cancellationToken);
            }
            catch
            {
                // Ignored - we only want to verify the logger call
            }

            // Assert
            mockLogger.Verify(
                l => l.Log(
                    LogLevel.Debug,
                    It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                    It.Is<It.IsAnyType>((v, t) => v.ToString().Contains("Tool requests")),
                    null,
                    It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception?, string>>()),
                Times.AtLeastOnce);
        }

        // A minimal fake HttpMessageHandler to avoid real HTTP calls
        private class FakeHttpMessageHandler : System.Net.Http.HttpMessageHandler
        {
            protected override Task<System.Net.Http.HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(System.Net.Http.HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
            {
                var response = new System.Net.Http.HttpResponseMessage(System.Net.HttpStatusCode.OK)
                {
                    Content = new System.Net.Http.StringContent("{\"choices\":[{\"tool_call\":true,\"tool_call_count\":1}]}")
                };
                return Task.FromResult(response);
            }
        }

        // Minimal stub for ChatHistory to satisfy parameter requirements
        private class ChatHistory : List<ChatMessageContent>
        {
        }

        // Minimal stub for ChatMessageContent to satisfy return type
        private class ChatMessageContent
        {
        }
    }
}

            // Act
            LoggerExtensions.LogDebug(mockLogger.Object, "Tool requests: {Requests}", 5);

            // Assert
            mockLogger.Verify(
                l => l.Log(
                    LogLevel.Debug,
                    It.IsAny<EventId>(),

                    It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception?, string>>()),

        }

        public void LogDebug_DoesNotLog_WhenLogLevelDebugDisabled()
        {
            // Arrange
            var mockLogger = new Mock<ILogger>();
            mockLogger.Setup(l => l.IsEnabled(LogLevel.Debug)).Returns(false);

            // Act
            LoggerExtensions.LogDebug(mockLogger.Object, "Tool requests: {Requests}", 5);

            // Assert
            mockLogger.Verify(
                l => l.Log(

                    It.IsAny<EventId>(),
